source.citation: Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Torrence, M.H. layers.meaning: Average fraction of time the Sun is visible from the surface (0 = never lit, 1 = always lit). Averaged over hourly time steps across 18.6 years (one lunar nodal precession cycle), modelled from LOLA polar topography (LOLA data 2009-07-13 to 2013-07-18), 2016-08 release. How partial visibility of the solar disc is counted was not checked here; the product page does not state a height above the surface, so treat it as at ground level (0 m).

layers.meaning: Average fraction of time the Earth is visible from the surface (0 = never, 1 = always). Averaged over hourly time steps across 18.6 years (one lunar nodal precession cycle), modelled from LOLA polar topography (LOLA data 2009-07-13 to 2013-07-18), 2016-08 release. Per the product notes Earth counts as visible when any part of its disc is unobscured, so this is slightly optimistic for radio-link planning; no height above the surface is stated, so treat it as at ground level (0 m).

layers.grid: row 0 = max y, col 0 = min x; identical to terrain sp_dem_L0
layers.resampling: area average of the 0/1 source mask, then threshold: 255 where at least half of the output pixel's area is PSR in the 120 m source (majority rule), else 0. PSRs smaller than about half a 297 m pixel are dropped.

source.citation: Mazarico, E., Neumann, G.A., Smith, D.E., Zuber, M.T., Torrence, M.H. layers.meaning: Permanently shadowed region: ground that never receives direct sunlight in the model. Averaged over hourly time steps across 18.6 years (one lunar nodal precession cycle), modelled from LOLA polar topography (LOLA data 2009-07-13 to 2013-07-18), 2016-08 release. Mask is at ground level and resampled from 120 m to 297 m by majority rule.
